summary: Ignace Municipal Airport (ZUC/CZUC) is a small regional airfield serving the township of Ignace in northwestern Ontario, Canada. Located along the Trans-Canada Highway corridor, it primarily supports general aviation, charter operations, and serves as a useful staging point for visitors exploring the vast boreal forest region. The airport sits at an elevation of approximately 1,435 feet and features a single asphalt runway, providing vital access to a remote area otherwise reachable only by road.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Ignace Municipal Airport?
A: The IATA code is ZUC and the ICAO code is CZUC.

Q: Does Ignace Municipal Airport have scheduled commercial service?
A: No, the airport does not currently offer scheduled commercial flights and primarily serves general aviation, charter, and private operations.

Q: Where is Ignace Municipal Airport located?
A: It is located near the town of Ignace in the Kenora District of northwestern Ontario, Canada, along the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 17).

Q: How many runways does the airport have?
A: The airport has a single paved runway suitable for small to medium general aviation aircraft.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a short drive south of the town of Ignace off Highway 17, making it easily accessible by car with on-site parking available. There is no public transit connection to the airport, so renting a vehicle or arranging a pickup in advance is recommended. Local taxi services in Ignace can be contacted ahead of time for arrivals, as they may not be readily available on-site.
local_tip: Visitors should fill up their fuel tanks in Ignace before heading further north or west, as the next reliable gas stations can be well over 100 km away in the surrounding wilderness areas—making a full tank upon arrival essential for exploring nearby lakes and parks.
